source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

05131.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Sebastian County moved 18 points toward the Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential vote. Trump carried it by 38 points; Cotton won it by 19, with 19,127 votes to Shoffner's 12,721. That is close to the statewide swing of 19 points and above the typical Arkansas county's 16. It ranks 17th of 75 by move, in a state where every county shifted left.

Turnout was 33,208 votes, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Craighead moved more (24 points), Saline slightly less (17) and Garland less (13).

05105.t:
Perry County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Cotton beat Shoffner here 2,244 to 875, a margin of 42 points, down from Trump's 58-point win over Harris. That is a 15-point move toward the Democrats, close to the typical Arkansas county (16 points) and slightly smaller than the state's 19-point swing, from R+31 to R+12. Every one of Arkansas's 75 counties moved left. Among similar counties, Clay moved about the same (15 points), Madison more (21) and Little River less (12).

Turnout fell sharply: 3,241 votes, 71% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the figures should hold.

All 75 Arkansas counties moved left; Clay ranks 45th.

Only 3,389 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar Arkansas counties, Fulton moved about as much (16 points), Stone a little less (13) and Sevier far more (31).

The shift sits almost exactly at the Arkansas norm: every one of the state's 75 counties moved left, the typical one by 16 points, and Drew ranks 43rd. Similar counties moved alike, with Columbia and Union each shifting 14 points, while Mississippi County swung 25. Turnout fell to 5,051 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05143.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Shoffner and Cotton, Washington County went from a 7-point Trump win in 2024 to an 18-point Shoffner win, 43,713 votes to 30,388. That 24-point move toward the Democrats ranks third among Arkansas's 75 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Arkansas county moved 16 points, and the statewide shift was 19 points. Washington is one of only two Arkansas counties that flipped from Trump to the Democrat.

Turnout was 76,041 votes, or 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties moved less: Desha 17 points, Crittenden 16 and St. Francis 12.

05007.t:
In Benton County, Republican Tom Cotton beat Democrat Hallie Shoffner in the U.S. Senate race 51,024 to 44,972, a margin of about 6 points. Donald Trump had carried the county by 27 points in 2024, so it moved 21 points toward the Democrats, slightly more than Arkansas's 19-point shift and well above the typical county's 16 in the state. All 75 Arkansas counties moved left, and Benton ranked eighth by size of move and second by votes cast. Similar counties moved less: Faulkner 20 points, Carroll 19 and Garland 13.

About 99,022 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

05037.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Cross County backed Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner 2,603 to 1,472, a 27-point margin. Trump carried it by 48 points in 2024, so the county moved 21 points toward the Democrats. That was more than the statewide shift of 19 points and the typical Arkansas county's 16, and it ranked 7th of 75 counties in a state where every county moved left. Similar counties moved less: Ashley 13 points, Howard 17 and Jackson 19. Cotton won statewide by 12.

Only 4,245 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05107.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Phillips County voted for Shoffner over Cotton by 24 points, 2,493 to 1,518, after backing Harris by 13 points in 2024. That 10-point move toward the Democrats is about half the state's 19-point shift. Phillips ranks 73rd of Arkansas's 75 counties by move. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 16 points. Among comparable counties, Chicot and Lee each moved 15 points, while Jefferson moved 9.

The county cast 4,152 votes, 84% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

05075.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Lawrence County moved 16 points toward the Democrats, from Trump's 64-point win in 2024 to a 48-point win for Cotton over Shoffner. Cotton took 2,757 votes to Shoffner's 907, with 99% of the expected vote counted. Turnout fell sharply: 3,877 ballots, 68% of the 5,692 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The shift was close to the typical Arkansas county's 16 points. All 75 counties moved left. The state as a whole moved 19. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Newton 15, Randolph 18 and Poinsett 20.

05011.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Tom Cotton carried Bradley County over Hallie Shoffner by 23 points, 1,379 votes to 844. Trump had won it by 39 points in 2024, so the county moved 16 points toward the Democrats, in line with the typical Arkansas county and a little less than the state's 19-point swing. All 75 of Arkansas's counties moved left; Bradley ranks 35th.

Turnout fell sharply: 2,311 votes, 72% of the 3,209 cast in 2024. With so many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Nevada moved 12 points, Lafayette 14 and Hempstead 17.

05009.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Democrat Shoffner and Republican Cotton, Boone County stayed firmly Republican but moved 16 points toward the Democrats. Cotton carried it 8,298 to 2,667, a margin of 49 points, down from Trump's 65-point margin in 2024. That move sits in the middle of Arkansas, where all 75 counties shifted left and the typical county moved 16 points. Among similar counties, Boone moved more than Cleburne (10 points) but less than Greene and Poinsett (20 each).

Turnout fell sharply. The 11,406 votes cast were 67% of the 2024 total of 17,112, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05091.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Cotton carried Miller County over Shoffner 7,276 to 3,133, a margin of 39 points. Trump had won it by 51 in 2024, so the county moved 12 points toward the Democrats. That is a smaller shift than in most of Arkansas, where every county moved left and the typical one moved 16 points. Miller ranks 59th of 75 by size of move. Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved further: Hot Spring 16 points, Pope 18 and Johnson 21.

Turnout fell sharply, to 10,710 votes from 15,803 in 2024, about 68% of the earlier total. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

05093.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Mississippi County gave Cotton 3,985 votes to Shoffner's 3,454, a Republican margin of 7 points. Trump carried it by 32 in 2024, so the county moved 25 points toward the Democrats, the second-largest shift among Arkansas's 75 counties. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 16 points, and Cotton won statewide by 12 after Trump's 31-point margin.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 7,681 votes, 72% of its 2024 total of 10,717, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved less: Carroll by 19 points, Drew by 15 and Union by 14.

05083.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Logan County stayed firmly with Republican Tom Cotton but by a smaller margin than in 2024. Cotton led Democrat Hallie Shoffner 3,893 to 1,390, a margin of 44 points, down from Trump's 62-point margin over Harris. That is an 18-point move toward the Democrats, slightly more than the typical Arkansas county's 16 points and close to the statewide shift of 19.

Turnout fell sharply, to 5,665 votes from 8,205, or 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Franklin moved more (23 points), while Sharp and Stone moved less (12 and 13).

05067.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Jackson County voted for Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by 30 points, 2,089 votes to 1,107. That is 19 points closer than Trump's 49-point win here in 2024, about the same as the statewide shift, as Cotton carried Arkansas by 12. All 75 Arkansas counties moved toward the Democrats. Jackson's move ranks 15th, larger than the typical county's 16 points in the state and 14 nationally. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Howard 17 points, Cross 21 and Lincoln 16.

Only 3,288 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05089.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Marion County voted for Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by 4,094 to 1,323, a margin of 50 points. Donald Trump carried it by 60 points in 2024, so the county moved 11 points toward the Democrats. That was a smaller shift than in most of Arkansas: every county moved left, the typical one by 16 points, and Marion ranks 67th of 75. Counties with similar 2024 results moved further, with Van Buren shifting 12 points and Yell and Madison about 21 each.

The county cast 5,597 votes, 71% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05031.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Craighead County voted for Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by about 14 points, 14,416 votes to 10,867. That is a shift of 24 points toward the Democrats from 2024, when Trump carried the county by 37. The swing ranks fourth among Arkansas's 75 counties, all of which moved left. It is well above the typical state move of 16 points and the statewide shift of 19. Similar counties moved less: Sebastian 18, Saline 17 and Garland 13.

Turnout fell sharply. The 26,180 votes cast were 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05111.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Poinsett County still went heavily for Cotton, 3,620 votes to 1,350 for Shoffner, a margin of 43 points. That was 20 points narrower than Trump's 64-point win over Harris here in 2024. The shift toward the Democrats was slightly larger than the state's 19-point move and above the typical Arkansas county's 16. Poinsett ranks 11th of 75 counties by move, and every county in the state moved left.

Turnout was 74% of the 2024 level, 5,233 ballots against 7,079, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Poinsett moved more than Randolph (18 points) and Sharp (12) but less than Franklin (23).

05005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hallie Shoffner and Tom Cotton, Baxter County stayed firmly Republican but shifted 10 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 57 points in 2024; Cotton won it by 47, with 10,230 votes to Shoffner's 3,597. That was one of Arkansas's smallest moves, 72nd of 75 counties, below the typical county's 16 points and the state's 19. Similar counties moved further: Crawford, Independence and Lonoke each shifted 16 or 17 points.

Turnout was 68% of the 2024 vote, 14,249 ballots against 20,954, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures should hold.

05061.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Howard County backed Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by 30 points, 2,043 votes to 1,064. That is 17 points closer than Donald Trump's 47-point margin here in 2024. Every one of Arkansas's 75 counties moved toward the Democrats. Howard's shift was a little larger than the typical county's 16 points but smaller than the state's 19. It ranks 27th in the state by move.

Turnout fell sharply. The 3,240 votes cast were 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties of similar size and 2024 lean, Cross moved 21 points, Jackson 19 and Ashley 13.

05051.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Tom Cotton (R) carried Garland County over Hallie Shoffner (D) by 23 points, 18,908 votes to 11,646. That is a 13-point move toward the Democrats from 2024, when Trump won here by 36. Statewide, Cotton won by 12 after Trump's 31-point margin, an Arkansas swing of 19 points.

Garland, seventh among the state's 75 counties by votes cast, moved less than most: it ranks 52nd, short of the typical Arkansas county's 16-point shift and the national 14. Sebastian, Craighead and Faulkner, similar in size and 2024 vote, moved 18, 24 and 20 points. About 31,602 votes were cast, three-quarters of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05045.t: Faulkner County swung toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, voting for Tom Cotton (R) over Hallie Shoffner (D) by 12 points, 21,990 to 17,002, after backing Trump by 32 points in 2024. That 20-point move was a little larger than Arkansas's statewide shift of 19 points and ranked 12th of the state's 75 counties, all of which moved left. It outpaced similar counties such as Sebastian (18 points), Union (14) and Garland (13). Turnout reached only 74% of the 2024 vote, with 40,306 ballots cast, still the fifth-most in the state. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

05115.t:
Pope County stayed solidly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by much less than in 2024. Cotton beat Shoffner 10,900 to 5,175, a margin of 34 points, after Trump carried the county by 52. That 18-point move toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical Arkansas county's 16 and the national typical move of 14, and close to the state's own 19-point shift. Every one of Arkansas's 75 counties moved left. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Lonoke 17 points, Hot Spring 16 and Miller 12.

Only 16,643 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05081.t:
Little River County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, with Cotton beating Shoffner 2,533 to 965, a margin of about 43 points. That is roughly 12 points narrower than Trump's 54-point win here in 2024. Every county in Arkansas moved toward the Democrats, the typical one by about 16 points, so Little River's shift was smaller than most; it ranks 64th of 75. Similar counties moved further, including Perry (15 points), Hot Spring (16) and Johnson (21).

Turnout was 3,684 votes, about three-quarters of the 4,899 cast in 2024. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Statewide, Cotton won by 12 points after Trump carried Arkansas by 31.

05095.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Monroe County moved about 14 points toward the Democrats, from a 16-point Trump win in 2024 to a 2-point Cotton edge over Shoffner. Cotton took 1,021 votes to Shoffner's 979, out of 2,067 cast with 99% of the expected vote counted. That shift is slightly smaller than the typical Arkansas county's 16-point move and the state's 19, ranking 50th of 75. Among similar counties, Ouachita moved 11 points, Clark 15 and Desha 17, enough there to flip it to a 12-point Democratic win.

Turnout was 85% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05073.t: In the U.S. Senate race, Lafayette County voted for Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by 1,113 votes to 665, a margin of 24 points. That is 14 points toward the Democrats from Donald Trump's 38-point win here in 2024. The shift was a little smaller than Arkansas's 19-point swing and the typical county's 16 points in a state where all 75 counties moved left, and about equal to the typical national move. Similar counties moved by 12 to 17 points. Only 1,840 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05027.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Columbia County went for Cotton over Shoffner by 22 points, 3,402 votes to 2,130. That is 14 points less Republican than its 36-point margin for Trump in 2024. The move matches the typical county nationally and falls just short of the typical Arkansas county (16 points). It ranks 47th of the state's 75 counties, all of which moved left.

Turnout fell sharply. The 5,720 votes cast were 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Drew by 15 points, Conway by 13 and Hempstead by 17.

05025.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Cleveland County gave Tom Cotton 1,780 votes to Hallie Shoffner's 454, a Republican margin of 57 points. That is 11 points narrower than Trump's 68-point margin in 2024. Every Arkansas county moved toward the Democrats, but Cleveland moved less than most, ranking 66th of 75. The typical county shifted 16 points, and the state shifted 19 as Cotton won by 12. Similar counties moved somewhat more: Prairie 13 points, Izard 12 and Newton 15.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 2,339 votes, 69% of its 2024 total of 3,374, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

05077.t:
Lee County voted for Shoffner over Cotton in the U.S. Senate race by 19 points, 1,188 votes to 807, with 99% of the expected vote counted. In 2024 it gave Harris a 4-point edge over Trump, so it moved 15 points toward the Democrats. That is close to the typical Arkansas county (+16) and slightly above the national typical move (+14). Every county in the state moved left. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Chicot +15, Crittenden +16 and St. Francis +12.

Turnout was 2,040, about 81% of the 2024 vote. With that many fewer ballots, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

05121.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Randolph County voted for Republican Tom Cotton over Democrat Hallie Shoffner by 46 points, 3,122 votes to 1,092. That is an 18-point move toward the Democrats from Donald Trump's 64-point win here in 2024. It is about the same as Arkansas's statewide shift of 19 points and a little more than the typical county's 16 in a state where all 75 counties moved left. Randolph ranks 18th by move. Counties with a similar 2024 vote and size ranged from Sharp's 12-point shift to Poinsett's 20.

Turnout was 67% of the 2024 vote, 4,441 ballots against 6,636, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

05137.t:
Stone County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Cotton beat Shoffner 3,101 to 999, a margin of 49 points, down from Trump's 62-point margin over Harris. That 13-point move toward the Democrats is smaller than the state's 19-point shift and the typical Arkansas county's 16, ranking 58th of 75 counties.

Turnout fell sharply: 4,290 votes were cast, 71% of the 6,030 in 2024. The count alone cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved more: Fulton 16 points, Clay 15 and Yell 21.
